faqs.q: What is Base64 encoding used for?
faqs.a: Base64 is designed to represent binary data in an ASCII string format, commonly used in email headers, HTTP authorization tokens, and data URIs.
No. Base64 is an encoding scheme, not an encryption technique. It does not provide cryptographic secrecy.
